description: A one-voice sample player holding twenty-five LinnDrum drum sounds in five banks, fired from a jack or from the button on the panel

params.text: Sets how much louder the sample plays when the accent input is high as the trigger arrives, up to 70% above the ordinary level
Chooses one of the five banks: Kick&Clap, Snare, Toms, Hat&crash and Extras
Plays the chosen sample once each time it is pressed
Sets the playback speed, 1 being the speed the sample was recorded at and 2 playing it eight times faster; the scale follows the cube of the setting
Chooses one of the five samples inside the bank
Turned past halfway, the sample is read a whole step at a time with no interpolation, which roughens it at speeds away from normal; below halfway it changes nothing
Shortens the sample with a straight fade to silence; fully anticlockwise it cuts the sound about a seventh of the way through, and almost fully clockwise the whole sample plays

inputs.text: Read at the moment the trigger arrives: above 0.5V the sample plays at the louder level set by the Accent knob
Plays the chosen sample once when it rises past 0.5V
Adds to the playback speed set by Tune, a fifth of the recorded speed per volt, with the total held at a twentieth of the recorded speed or above
Stops the sample dead while it is above 0.5V
Read at the moment the trigger arrives: above 0.5V the sample plays backwards
Makes the fade quicker, a tenth of the decay knob's travel per volt
Steps on through all twenty-five samples from wherever the bank and sample knobs have left the choice, 2.5 samples per volt

outputs.text: The chosen sample, five times the level it is stored at and half as much again, so a full-scale sample peaks near 7.5V and more with accent

notes: The screen across the top shows the name of the chosen bank and the name of the chosen sample. It is a display rather than a control and cannot be clicked.
The decay knob comes up fully anticlockwise, which cuts every sample off about a seventh of the way through. Turn it almost all the way up to hear a whole sample.
